solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not as heavy as a barge

definitions.meaning: weighing less, the comparative of light
a flat-bottomed boat used to ferry goods to and from ships in harbour

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the comparative adjective of weight; the other is a noun for a cargo boat unloading ships.

clue.text: They stand in place around front of mausoleum

indicators.note: around means the word for place goes round the chosen letter

parts.note: locus is Latin for place and used in English for a location

indicators.note: front of takes the first letter of mausoleum

explanation.surface: Mourners stand around a mausoleum.
explanation.definitionFit: Locums are doctors or clergy who deputise for absent colleagues, temporary substitutes.

clue.text: European enthusiasm for weapon employed in naval warfare

parts.note: a Greek is a European
fire is passion or enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A European's passion for a weapon of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Byzantine forces used an incendiary liquid of that name against enemy ships.

clue.text: It's loosely about a French city

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the French article
loosely means the letters are loosened and reordered

parts.note: un is French for a

explanation.surface: A vague claim about some French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' reshuffles the apostrophised IT'S, its apostrophe ignored, and 'about' wraps the result round the French article; 'a French' tempts as a description of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia.

clue.text: Cross to receive bishop in house of famous outlaw

indicators.note: to receive means the cross takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix or cross
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cross is brought into the home of a legendary bandit.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the English folk hero who robbed the rich to give to the poor.

clue.text: Decorated with crude tapestries originally

parts.note: crude means rough, unrefined

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word tapestries

explanation.surface: A wall hung with rough, primitive tapestries.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrought is the old past participle of work: metal or fabric wrought is worked into ornamental form, hence decorated.

clue.text: Complete dump by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for dump is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a dump is a dismal place, a hole

explanation.surface: A total tip, from what you hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole means entire, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Favouring traditional methods of former coach

parts.note: old means former, as in an old flame
to school someone is to coach or train them

explanation.surface: A retired coach prefers the time-honoured ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-school describes a conservative person or style keeping to established ways.

clue.text: Spain forbidding earlier form of dance music

indicators.note: earlier puts the word for forbidding before the Spain letter

parts.note: grim means stern and forbidding
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Spain banning an early style of dance music.
explanation.definitionFit: Grime is a British electronic genre that grew from UK garage in early-2000s London.

clue.text: Aim to block shot with it

indicators.note: to block means sit inside, so the aim goes into the word for shot

parts.note: a shot is an attempt, a try
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A defender tries to stop a shot at goal.
explanation.definitionFit: With it is a slangy phrase for fashionable and up to date.

clue.text: In prison Ellen oddly neglected to be attentive to personal hygiene

indicators.note: In places what follows inside the word for prison

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: the odd-position letters of Ellen are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Ellen, jailed, has let her personal hygiene slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly neglected' keeps only the even-placed letters of the name, and 'In' at the start signals that pair going inside the prison word. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone washed and tidy is described as clean, the plain adjective for good hygiene.

clue.text: Dido bears outrageously fierce verbal attack

indicators.note: behaving outrageously means wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Queen Dido endures something shocking in the story of Carthage.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside, originally a volley from all guns on one side of a ship, is figuratively a forceful tirade.

clue.text: Forms filled in by a nurse have ultimately to be understandable

indicators.note: the nurse's letters go inside the word for forms, filling it

parts.note: to form something is to make it, so forms gives makes
SEN is State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of have

explanation.surface: Paperwork completed by a nurse ought to be legible in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filled in by' puts the nurse inside the verb just before its final S; 'ultimately' adds the last letter of 'have'. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being coherent or intelligible is this two-word phrase.

clue.text: Daughter following Native American system of belief

indicators.note: following puts the daughter's letter after the people's name

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American and First Nations people
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter adopts the faith of a Native American nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of religious beliefs or a guiding doctrine.

clue.text: Lie about taking fellow's sock

indicators.note: taking adds the next letter on to the end
about means turned round, so the word for lie is read backwards

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
F is an abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A liar's tale involves some man's stocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sock and biff are both informal words for a punch or a hard blow.

clue.text: Lucky on account of letter to the head being withdrawn

parts.note: for means on account of, as in famous for

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: eta is a Greek letter
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Lucky, since a letter to the headteacher was retracted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being withdrawn' reverses ETANUT to TUNATE; 'to' just links the two pieces. 'the head' misleads toward a headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortunate and lucky are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: The head boy initially missing on account of a violent beating

indicators.note: missing means the boy's letter is absent from the slang word

parts.note: bonce is British slang for the head

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of boy

parts.note: over can mean on account of, as in a row over money

explanation.surface: A head boy gets thrashed but is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives B; 'missing' removes it from BONCE, leaving ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A once-over, usually a quick look, is also slang for a thrashing, like a going-over.

clue.text: Depressing to find what supporters of those losing may do

definitions.text: what supporters of those losing may do
definitions.meaning: fans of a losing side applaud less, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means gloomy; split into two words it says fans of a beaten team give less encouragement.

clue.text: Shocking for fellow taken in by Georgia over promises to pay

indicators.note: taken in by means the fellow sits inside the other pieces
over in a down clue means turned upward, so the letters reverse

parts.note: GE is the country code for Georgia
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt
Reg is a man's name, standing for a fellow

explanation.surface: A man duped by Georgia over unpaid debts.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgia here is the country (code GE), not the US state; 'over' turns it upward in this down clue, and 'taken in by' sets the fellow between it and the IOUs.
explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means outstandingly bad, flagrant.

clue.text: Resent having to plead with Dickens character

parts.note: to beg is to plead
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: Someone resents having to plead with a figure from Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge is to resent someone having or getting something.

clue.text: Learning about depressed wife leaving earlier

indicators.note: earlier puts the trimmed word first
leaving means the wife's letter goes from the word for depressed

parts.note: depressed means low in spirits
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A man takes up study after his low-spirited wife walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Lore is traditional knowledge and teaching handed down, a body of learning.

clue.text: Familiar with American chaps ignoring Miles

indicators.note: ignoring means the letter for miles is left out

parts.note: Ed and Tom are two chaps' names

explanation.surface: Some American men snub a man named Miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaps' is plural, so two names are needed: ED and TOM, losing M.
explanation.definitionFit: Being accustomed to something means being familiar with it.

clue.text: Damage caused by mischievous child is on display

indicators.note: in a down clue is on means placed above, so the child comes first

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
to air is to display or show openly

explanation.surface: A naughty child causes damage, and it's there for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or damage.

clue.text: Holy man unhappy with homoerotic urges at first

parts.note: sad means unhappy

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letters of homoerotic and urges

explanation.surface: An ascetic is troubled by forbidden desires.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu holy man or wandering ascetic.

clue.text: Records showing Head of Charterhouse residing in town

indicators.note: residing in places the chosen letter inside the town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, England

indicators.note: Head of takes the first letter of Charterhouse

explanation.surface: School records show a headmaster living in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Charterhouse is an English public school, so 'Head' suggests its headmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Discs are gramophone records, vinyl.

clue.text: Start game uncertain of plan

indicators.note: uncertain letters are unsettled, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: Begin a contest without knowing the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme or plan, often to deceive.

clue.text: Penny joins Bill in the London area for a short time

indicators.note: in places both pieces inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: SE is South East, the region of England around London

indicators.note: joins puts the penny next to the bill

parts.note: AC is account, a bill

explanation.surface: A penny is paid to settle a London bill briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Space can mean an interval of time, as in in the space of a minute.

clue.text: Make fun of supporters on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means the word for supporters is heard, not seen

parts.note: tees support golf balls before driving

explanation.surface: Mock fans when broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease is to mock playfully.

clue.text: Damage the reputation of princess's attendant over a bit of rowdiness

parts.note: Di was the familiar name of Princess Diana, so princess's gives Di's

indicators.note: over means the attendant is spread over, enclosing, what follows

parts.note: a page is a young attendant

indicators.note: a bit of takes the first letter of rowdiness

explanation.surface: A royal servant's rowdy behaviour tarnishes the princess's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means covering: the attendant wraps round A and the first letter of rowdiness. Di is Princess Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage is to belittle or speak slightingly of, harming standing.

clue.text: Meeting place for American soldiers in Georgia

indicators.note: in puts the soldiers inside the abbreviation for Georgia

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
OR is other ranks, enlisted soldiers

explanation.surface: A rendezvous point for US troops stationed in Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the public square of an ancient Greek city, used for assembly and markets.

clue.text: Disgusting display of emotion seen by former pupil

indicators.note: seen by means the emotional outburst stands beside, after, the former pupil

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school
making a scene is a public display of emotion

explanation.surface: An old boy witnesses a revolting emotional outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive or repugnant, morally disgusting.

clue.text: Meaning to keep page on Russia's foremost poet

indicators.note: on puts the following letter after the rest
to keep means the word for meaning holds the page inside

parts.note: sense is meaning, as in the sense of a word

indicators.note: foremost takes the first letter of Russia's

explanation.surface: Something meaning to keep a page about Russia's leading poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts P inside SENSE after its S, giving SPENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.
